binding_legend: constraint: may not be contradicted; default: convention supplied it, may be replaced with something more specific; free: nothing known, fill it

3-0a.primary_decision_axis.label: which of the seven guests to accuse of the murder
3-0a.primary_decision_axis.description: Having gathered what the clues and the guests' lies support, name one of the seven as the killer — with the Kernel insisting the wrong person must be a live, pickable option, not just the right one.

axes.label: which guest's lie to press or which clue to follow next

3-0b.protagonist_identity.role: new housekeeper at a snowbound country house

3-0b.epistemic_gap.description: who murdered the master of the house in his locked study, and how, given that all seven guests are lying about something

channels: which guests' lies have been exposed

conflicts.summary: The decision is which of seven guests to accuse, while the thematic axis is truth versus protective discretion; naming guest A rather than guest B is not recognizably picking a pole of that axis, and accusing wrongly is a mistake, not a choice of discretion.

3d tags an invited flashback to the murder night as interactive, but no decision inside that flashback appears in 3-0a's primary or secondary axes, and 3-0b's gap does not place anything to be learned there; 3-0a's secondary axis and 3d's interactive flag are both strong_inference.

unresolved: C9: whether the invited flashback to the murder night is a played interactive scene (3d) or recalled exposition with no decisions (3-0a lists none inside it); if played, its choices must be defined and constrained so what the housekeeper saw stays fixed for fair-play clueing.

C3 flag: the thematic axis (truth vs. protective discretion) is genre-supplied and does not map onto the accusation branch; the premise-expansion phase must either supply a stated value tension that the accusation can express or treat theme as coloring rather than branch structure.
